title: Trumpet held at the mouth

source.source_title: [Amateur films: Ivan Besse collection: Britton, South Dakota 1938-39] (Part VI)
source.why_this_clip: A man in a dark suit is seen in profile playing a trumpet held level with the bell pointing left. The trumpet bobs as he plays and tilts upward around 3.5 s before settling. The clip has no cuts, so this is one continuous 5 s stretch; the player is labelled because the trumpet alone is small in frame.

source_selection.evidence: Builder inspected sixteen raw source frames across the provisional event in preflight-source.jpg; no cut/dissolve observed inside retained interval. Normal-speed playback unrun.

assembly_summary: Player holds trumpet at his mouth, makes small instrument bobs, lifts slightly near3.5s, then settles.
review_note: Fresh still review v1: native identity met; source framing/pose not met. The horn’s bell occupies far too much vertical space and hangs well below the supporting hand; the source bell is a small opening on a slender horn aimed left and slightly down from the player’s mouth. This changes the sampled playing pose despite the similar horizontal placement. Recognition classifier, audited final mask fit, four verified contacts and actual normal-speed playback remain unrun or unmet. No training ran.
